Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, I'm a first-year associate at a local firm, and my senior associate has been there for three years. A few weeks ago, I wasn't feeling well and threw up right after waking up. I notified her that I wouldn't be coming to work because I was sick. She was a bit disappointed but allowed me to take a sick leave. That's good because she understood that I was unwell. During my sick leave, I sent a few emails to our client as she had requested the previous day. I was trying to get some sleep because I wasn't feeling well. However, my senior associate kept texting me with things I needed to do. I tried to ignore her messages and turned off my phone's notifications so I could rest. After about an hour, she called me and told me I had to send her a file immediately regarding the client's data, which she didn't have on her laptop. I sent her the files and asked if she needed anything else since I was going to the doctor and wouldn't be bringing my laptop with me. She said that was all for now. I went to the doctor, who told me I was overworked because I had been working overtime until 2-3 AM for the past two months and needed some rest. On my way home, my senior associate texted me again, asking me to get our client's billing information, something she could have done herself since she has their contacts. I did as she asked and forwarded her the information. I got home, took the prescribed medicine, and fell asleep. When I woke up, I was shocked to find my phone with two missed calls and 30 new messages from her, giving me work to do from home. I felt it was a little unfair of her to give me work while I was on sick leave, so I ignored the messages and didn't reply. Now, the question is: Am I in the wrong for not replying to her texts? Is it right or wrong? Let me think about this step by step. First, I was sick and needed rest. I notified my senior associate about my condition and took a sick leave, which is appropriate. She allowed me to take the leave, so she understood that I was unwell. During my sick leave, she kept texting me with work-related tasks. I tried to ignore her messages to get some rest, which is important for recovery. She called me, and I responded to her urgent request by sending her the necessary files. After that, I informed her that I was going to the doctor and wouldn't be bringing my laptop, implying that I wouldn't be available for further work. Despite this, she continued to text me with more work, even though I was on sick leave and had already provided her with the necessary information. I felt it was unfair for her to assign me work while I was unwell and needed rest. Ignoring her messages was my way of setting boundaries to ensure I could recover properly. However, not replying might have come across as disrespectful or unprofessional, especially since she is my senior associate. On the other hand, she should have respected my sick leave and given me the space I needed to recover. Assigning me work while I was unwell was not considerate of my health and well-being. In conclusion, while ignoring her messages might seem like the right thing to do to prioritize my health, it could also be seen as unprofessional. It's a tough situation because I needed rest, but I also have a responsibility to communicate effectively with my senior associate, even if it's just to let her know that I'm unavailable to work due to my illness. Maybe the best approach would have been to respond to her initial messages, explain that I was unwell and on sick leave, and politely decline to take on more work until I recovered. This way, I would have maintained professionalism while also taking care of my health. Overall, it's a balance between taking care of oneself and fulfilling professional responsibilities. In this case, I think it's important to communicate clearly and set boundaries to ensure both personal well-being and professional integrity.
